title: Synthetic Customer Workload Lab for Embedding Drift & Provider Stability Signals
creator: Claire Liu
description: Set up a lightweight, reproducible lab to generate synthetic customer workloads that represent latency-sensitive, domain-specific usage (e.g., retail conversational search + RAG, customer support triage, and vector search for catalogs). Use this to measure: embedding drift across providers and quantized variants, API stability (errors, latency spikes, throttling behavior), and cost-latency-quality tradeoffs. The output will feed a new set of signals for the model landscape tracker and a dashboard for prioritizing model onboarding / fallback pairings.
background: We get fragmented signals from benchmarks (latency and token cost) and anecdotal customer reports about model regressions and provider flakiness. Existing datasets focus on synthetic microbenchmarks or single-endpoint stress tests; we lack a compact, repeatable workload that mimics realistic customer patterns across regions and payload shapes. A field lab with controlled personas and workload generators will let PMs and SREs correlate provider behavior with business-impact metrics.
objectives: Define 4 canonical synthetic personas and query patterns (Retail RAG shopper, Tier-1 support triage, Knowledge-base short-form search, Large-batch embedding refresh)
Create workload generators that vary key dimensions: sequence length, context window reuse, embedding batch sizes, and prefix cache reuse
Run cross-provider probes (hosted Redwood variants, two open-model hosts, and one private on-prem snapshot) across 3 regions to collect stability and latency distributions
Produce a compact signal set (embedding-drift score, API-flakiness index, median p95 latency delta, cost-per-successful-query) for the model landscape tracker
deliverables: Automated probe harness (reproducible script + small CI job) that runs 1-hour probes per provider/region
Signal export format (CSV/JSON) ingested by the landscape tracker
Dashboard mock and slice definitions for prioritization (SLA breach risk, fallback candidate list)
tasks: Draft persona templates and sample utterances (PM) — Claire
Prototype workload runner using existing perf-harness snippets (Eng) — assign runtime eng
Select provider endpoints and model variants for initial sweep (PM + Research)
Define metrics and simple scoring functions (embedding distance drift over time; API error burst detection)
Run baseline sweeps for 3 regions and collect first dataset
Validate signal ingestion into the landscape tracker and sanity-check dashboard visuals
success_metrics: Automated 1-hour probe runs produce consistent CSV outputs in >90% of runs
Embedding drift metric identifies known regression introduced in prior model changes (sanity check)
Dashboard enables a ranked list of fallback candidates for at least 2 critical enterprise customers
We detect at least one cross-provider flaky pattern (error spike or p95 jump) during the initial sweep or within the first two weeks
acceptance_criteria: Workload spec reviewed and approved by product & one runtime engineer
Probe harness runs end-to-end in CI against a mock provider and produces the defined export format
First cross-provider sweep uploaded to the model landscape tracker and visible on the dashboard mock
